record.paper_title: Conformally invariant scaling limits: an overview and a collection of problems
record.original_question: Fix n ≥ 1 and let T be a uniformly random tree contained in a planar grid G that contains the origin and has exactly n vertices. Determine the growth rate of the expected diameter of T. After rescaling graph distances so that the expected or median diameter is 1, determine whether the law of T has a limit as n tends to infinity, and if so describe the geometric and topological properties of that limit.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8. What is the growth rate of the expected diameter of such a tree? If we rescale the tree so that the expected (or median) diameter is 1, is there a limit for the law of the tree as n → ∞? What are its geometric and topological properties? Can the limit be determined?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = Z^2 be the planar square lattice, viewed as a graph with edges between nearest-neighbor vertices. A lattice tree in G is a finite connected subgraph of G that contains no cycles (equivalently, a finite subtree of G). Fix an integer n ≥ 1 and let T_n be a uniformly random lattice tree in G that contains the origin and has exactly n vertices.

(a) Determine the growth rate, as n → ∞, of the expected diameter E[diam(T_n)], where diam(T_n) is the maximum graph distance (within T_n) between two vertices of T_n.

(b) Rescale T_n by dividing all graph distances by a factor a_n chosen so that the expected (or median) diameter of the rescaled tree equals 1. Viewed as a random compact metric space (for instance with the Gromov–Hausdorff topology, or as a random embedded subset of the plane after rescaling Z^2 by a_n), does the law of the rescaled T_n converge to a limit as n → ∞?

(c) If such a scaling limit exists, describe its geometric and topological properties (e.g. Hausdorff dimension, whether it is a topological tree, its degree structure, conformal/rotational symmetries, and whether it can be identified explicitly).
artifact.status_search_result: In sufficiently high dimensions (d large, or spread-out models above the upper critical dimension 8), the scaling limit of uniform lattice trees is known to be Aldous's integrated super-Brownian excursion (ISE), confirming Aldous's conjecture. In two dimensions, however, the growth rate of the diameter of a uniformly random n-vertex lattice tree and the existence/identification of a scaling limit remain open; no proof of convergence (only conjectures of conformal invariance for related planar tree models) appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: The Scaling Limit of Lattice Trees in High Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Above eight dimensions, the scaling limit of sufficiently spread-out lattice trees is the variant of super-Brownian motion known as integrated super-Brownian excursion (ISE).
status_evidence.claim: High-dimensional case of the analogous lattice-tree scaling limit problem is resolved, leaving the low-dimensional (planar) case open.

status_evidence.title: Scaling limit for the random walk on critical lattice trees
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to address critical lattice trees primarily in high dimensions, with two-dimensional scaling limits remaining conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: Current research treats lattice-tree scaling limits in high dimensions; the planar case is not established.
